Officer's narrative
On a weekday afternoon in Pasadena, Texas, I responded to a two-vehicle collision involving a sideswipe durnig a
lane change. Driver 1 was operating a sedan in the center lane when the vehicle to the left, driven by Driver 2, moved
into the same space and made contact along the driver's side. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy for
the sedan, and the vehicle was registered to the same address. Driver 1 reported a concussion and was transported
to a local hospital for evaluation. A passenger was also in the sedan, and both the passenger and Driver 1 confirmed
that Driver 1 was behind the wheel at the time of the impact. No independent witnesses were located at the scene.
Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the left side of the sedan and the right rear quarter panel of the
second vehicle, and the visible damage is generally consistent with the reported impact. Neither driver reported prior
damage to either vehicle, and none was observed. The reported injury is consistent with the type and force of a
lateral collision of this kind. Both drivers were issued citations pending further review.
</page>

- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- occupants_listed: How many people does the police report list in the insured vehicle (Vehicle 1)? The rating is a whole number. Allowed: a whole number.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.
